independence_caveat: Same model family as the other reviewers; agreement is reading consistency, not independent validation.

findings.finding: The versioned build script exists, explicitly removes and writes .build.sha256, and rebuilt an isolated package copy successfully with exit code 0, so the executable regeneration path is present.
findings.source_location: lines 24-27 and 43-56; isolated-copy execution in scratch dir
findings.test: Run bash -n on the script, execute it against an isolated copy, and verify that .build.sha256 is created with the emitted PDF hash.
findings.reasoning: The script documents the checksum effect at lines 24-27 and implements it at lines 43-56. With the available efc-tex:2026 Docker image, the isolated build returned 0 and produced .build.sha256 containing a 64-character SHA-256 digest. The repository package itself was not modified.

findings.finding: The distributed package has no .build.sha256, and its .tex and PDF have the same filesystem mtime, so the package offers neither checksum readback nor a decisive mtime test for PDF freshness.
findings.source_location: package-root inventory; ai_manifest.json lines 18-61; stat output for .tex and PDF
findings.test: Check for package-root .build.sha256 and compare stat mtimes for the .tex and PDF files.
findings.reasoning: The package contains 11 tracked files and ai_manifest.json does not list .build.sha256. Both source and PDF report mtime 2026-09-22 17:09:55.343672104 UTC, so mtime ordering cannot establish whether the PDF is stale. The embedded PDF CreationDate is 2026-09-21 10:54:24 UTC, which indicates an older embedded build time but is not by itself conclusive stale-source evidence because the package files may have been exported together.

findings.finding: Two successive builds of unchanged .tex both exited 0 but produced different PDF hashes and different /CreationDate and /ID values, confirming the manuscript's byte-for-byte reproducibility gap.
findings.source_location: script line 27 and two isolated rebuild outputs in scratch dir
findings.test: Run efc_pdf_bygg.sh twice without changing the source and compare .build.sha256, PDF SHA-256, embedded CreationDate, and trailer ID.
findings.reasoning: The first isolated build produced one hash and the second a different one, and cmp confirmed the PDFs were not byte-identical. The regenerated PDF metadata changed from the first run to the second, demonstrating the timestamp/trailer nondeterminism described by the manuscript. This contradicts the build script's line-27 comment that output is deterministic given the .tex, but it supports the manuscript's explicit statement that byte-for-byte reproducibility remains open.

findings.finding: The clean build log contains 13 Overfull hbox diagnostics and one h-to-ht float-placement warning, matching the manuscript's disclosure of current layout warnings.
findings.test: Count Overfull hbox and float specifier changed diagnostics in the log generated by the isolated build.
findings.reasoning: The versioned Docker build completed successfully, and its retained LaTeX log contains 13 overfull-hbox messages and a LaTeX Warning: 'h' float specifier changed to 'ht'. The manuscript does not claim warning-free layout, so this part of C12 is accurate.

findings.finding: The package contains no src/, data/, or examples/, and its complete 11-file manifest contains no executable fit code or dataset, supporting the scoped statement that no new fit is executed by this package.
findings.test: Inventory the package recursively, check for src, data, and examples, and inspect every path listed in ai_manifest.json.
findings.reasoning: The package has only metadata, documentation, bibliography, JSON-LD, LaTeX, and PDF artifacts; the three directories named by the manuscript are absent. This verifies the narrow absence claim for the submitted package, but cannot rule out a fit performed externally or in an earlier source package.

findings.finding: The claimed post-freeze full-stack ordering is only partially honored: Git history adds the manuscript and PDF first and metadata or manifest files later, but the current package stops without the promised src/, data/, and examples/ stages.
findings.test: Review git log --reverse for the package, inspect the named commit file additions, and check whether src, data, or examples exists in the current package.
findings.reasoning: The initial 750a2366 commit added the manuscript and PDF, 90c20672 added authored metadata/package files, and later commits generated and fixed ai_manifest.json. That supports the coarse text-before-metadata sequence, but the promised full AI-friendly stack is not present because no source, data, or examples stage exists in the distributed package.
